title: the WSG precautions and perils slice with Table 39 - the Table 38 column semantics seam (start, refuel, wind resistance, capacity, visibility and the warmth wind rules), the fuel availability grids and the fire safety rules, printed p. 66
audit_label: R475 WSG fuel and fire safety pin audit
audit_comment: The Table 39 grids (the five terrains by four temperate seasons and the six terrains by four climate modifiers), the Table 38 column semantics (the start discipline with the tools and wind gates, the refuel shrink rule, the wind resistance semantics, the capacity doubling and clustering reductions, the visibility reductions and line-of-sight rulings, the warmth safe-distance and wind-modifier rules with the book own worked example) and the fire safety prose are audit examples.

banner.title: R475: the WSG PRECAUTIONS AND PERILS slice with TABLE 39, printed p. 66 - the fifth camping-arc round and the fifth TABLE ROUND of the arc, riding the Table 38 column semantics seam unpinned by R474 (whose boxes covered only the p. 65 grids): the start discipline (2d20 rounds for a character without the fire-building proficiency assuming tools, dry fuel and a breeze of no more than 15 mph; wind over 15 mph or wet fuel means 3d20; no start without tools for the unproficient; no start in wind over 30 mph without magic), the refuel semantics (a fire not refueled in time shrinks to the next lower size; a small fire never goes out within three turns but provides no warmth), the wind resistance semantics (unprotected fires only; falter and flicker with no warmth over the rated velocity; the spread chance to an uncontrollable fire), the capacity semantics (six men at 10 feet from a small fire, doubling per additional 10 feet to 12 men at 20; clustering diminishes by one-third at five feet, one-half at three feet and two-thirds at one foot: 4, 3 and 2 characters), the visibility semantics (yards in moonlight or darkness, one-third off in twilight and one-half off in daylight; the 540-yard large-fire flame; the glow through moderately dense forest; the steep-hill blockage; the smoke reveal), the warmth semantics (the 80-degree minimum safe distance, five segments to move away, three feet from a medium fire and five from a large, the 10-mph calm assumption, windward warmth minus 5 degrees per 10 mph or fraction, leeward safe distance plus 10 feet or one increment whichever is less, and the book own 30-mph medium-fire example: 20 degrees at 20 feet on the windward side instead of 30, 10 feet on the leeward side instead of 3), Table 39 in TWO grids (availability of fuel by terrain and season for a temperate climate: desert 20/20/20/20, forest 70/100/100/100, hills 40/70/70/60, plains 50/70/80/70, swamp 40/30/30/40; and the climate modifiers: desert -20/-10/-10/-20, forest -100/-30/+30/+30, hills -30/-20/+10/+20, mountains -40/-30/+20/+30, plains -60/-40/+20/+20, swamp -40/-20/+10/+20), the every-two-turns further checks, and the start of precautions and perils (no safe fire, the untended conflagration, the cardinal rules, the first rule: no fire on combustibles, 1-3 turns to clear, sparks 100 feet in a strong wind), printed p. 66.
banner.provenance: Ground truth two-way on the prose and the uncontested Table 39 cells, no physical-page reads: the user-run Termux tesseract text of printed p. 66 (p66_full.txt, p66_tsv.tsv) vs the pdf embedded text layer (pdftotext -layout, pdf page 67, p66_pdfy.txt). The two readers AGREE on all prose numbers: the 15-mph start breeze and the 3d20-instead-of-2d20 escalation, the 30-mph magical bar, the three-turn small-fire refuel grace, the 10-foot capacity base with the doubling to 12 men and the one-third, one-half and two-thirds clustering cuts with the 4/3/2 example, the 540-yard large-fire visibility with the one-third twilight and one-half daylight reductions, the 80-degree safe distance with the five segments and the 3-foot medium and 5-foot large burns, the 10-mph warmth assumption with the 5-degrees-per-10-mph windward cut and the 10-feet-or-one-increment leeward add, the full 30-mph worked example (20 degrees at 20 feet windward instead of 30, 10 feet leeward instead of 3), the temperate fuel grid for desert, forest, plains and swamp, the climate modifier grid for desert, forest, mountains, plains and swamp, the every-two-turns recheck and the 1-3 turn clearing time with 100-foot spark carry. CONTESTED: the HILLS rows of BOTH Table 39 grids - the pdf text layer DROPPED the hills rows from both grids entirely, and tesseract garbles them (the temperate autumn cell as a wide low-confidence blob, the four modifier cells as near-zero-confidence noise). The standing vision-on-png settler was applied TWICE with independent prompts, and BOTH reads AGREE EXACTLY: temperate hills 40/70/70/60 and climate modifiers -30/-20/+10/+20 - the R471/R473 two-vision-read precedent, with the second read calibrated against the neighboring rows. A web search for an independent online copy of the table found none. The settled rows are also plausible against their neighbors: the hills arctic -30 sits between forest -100 and mountains -40, and the hills modifiers match swamp on the three warmer columns.
banner.sentinel: All 44 Table 39 cells pinned (the 20 temperate cells and the 24 climate-modifier cells, both hills rows vision-settled); the Table 38 column semantics, the worked wind example and the fire safety prose are audit examples.

consts.name: wflStartBreezeMax
consts.comment: the start discipline assumes the fire is exposed to a breeze of no more than 15 mph

consts.name: wflStartDie
consts.comment: the start roll die: d20

consts.name: wflStartDice
consts.comment: a character without the fire-building proficiency starts a fire in 2d20 rounds

consts.name: wflHardStartDice
consts.comment: in wind over 15 mph or with wet fuel the time needed to start the fire is 3d20 instead

consts.name: wflNoStartWindMax
consts.comment: no character can start a fire in a wind of more than 30 mph without magical assistance

consts.name: wflSmallRefuelGrace
consts.comment: a small fire will not go out if it is not refueled within three turns

consts.name: wflCapBaseFeet
consts.comment: capacity is measured for characters bedded down at 10 feet from the fire

consts.name: wflSmallCapAt10
consts.comment: six men can bed down in a rough circle 10 feet away from a small fire

consts.name: wflSmallCapAt20
consts.comment: the same small fire will warm 12 men equally at 20 feet

consts.name: wflCapStepFeet
consts.comment: a fire capacity doubles for each additional 10 feet of distance

consts.name: wflDimFiveNum
consts.comment: clustering at five feet diminishes capacity by one-third: numerator

consts.name: wflDimFiveDen
consts.comment: clustering at five feet diminishes capacity by one-third: denominator

consts.name: wflDimThreeNum
consts.comment: clustering at three feet diminishes capacity by one-half: numerator

consts.name: wflDimThreeDen
consts.comment: clustering at three feet diminishes capacity by one-half: denominator

consts.name: wflDimOneNum
consts.comment: clustering at one foot diminishes capacity by two-thirds: numerator

consts.name: wflDimOneDen
consts.comment: clustering at one foot diminishes capacity by two-thirds: denominator

consts.name: wflClusterFiveMax
consts.comment: four characters can bed down within five feet of a small fire

consts.name: wflClusterThreeMax
consts.comment: three characters can cluster within three feet of the fire

consts.name: wflClusterOneMax
consts.comment: two characters can be within one foot of a small fire at the same time

consts.name: wflLargeVisYards
consts.comment: the flame of a large fire is easily visible at night from 540 yards away on a flat, featureless plain

consts.name: wflTwilightNum
consts.comment: in twilight conditions the visibility figure is reduced by one-third: numerator

consts.name: wflTwilightDen
consts.comment: the twilight visibility reduction: denominator

consts.name: wflDaylightNum
consts.comment: in daylight the visibility figure is reduced by one-half: numerator

consts.name: wflDaylightDen
consts.comment: the daylight visibility reduction: denominator

consts.name: wflSafeWarmthDegrees
consts.comment: the minimum safe distance is the distance at which the air temperature is raised by 80 degrees

consts.name: wflMoveAwaySegments
consts.comment: a character closer than the safe distance must move away promptly, within five segments, or may suffer damage

consts.name: wflMediumSafeFt
consts.comment: an unprotected character cannot remain closer than three feet from a medium fire without being burned

consts.name: wflLargeSafeFt
consts.comment: an unprotected character cannot remain closer than five feet from a large fire without being burned

consts.name: wflWarmCalmWindMax
consts.comment: the warming capabilities assume the fire is not exposed to wind of more than 10 mph

consts.name: wflWindwardDegStep
consts.comment: on the side facing the wind the warmth is reduced by 5 degrees per step

consts.name: wflWindwardMphStep
consts.comment: the windward warmth reduction applies for every 10 mph or fraction thereof of additional velocity

consts.name: wflLeewardFeetStep
consts.comment: on the side facing away from the wind the safe distance is increased by 10 feet or one table increment, whichever is less

consts.name: wflExWindMph
consts.comment: the worked example: a medium fire blazing away in a 30-mph north wind

consts.name: wflExWindwardDeg
consts.comment: the windward-side sleeper 20 feet away benefits from only a 20-degree increase

consts.name: wflExCalmDeg
consts.comment: the calm-wind warmth of the medium fire at 20 feet is 30 degrees

consts.name: wflExLeewardFt
consts.comment: the leeward-side sleeper must be at least 10 feet away in the example

consts.name: wflExCalmSafeFt
consts.comment: the calm-wind safe distance for a medium fire is 3 feet

consts.name: wflClearMinTurns
consts.comment: it takes from 1 turn for a single character to clear an area

consts.name: wflClearMaxTurns
consts.comment: up to 3 turns, at the Dungeon Master discretion, to clear an area before building a fire

consts.name: wflSparkCarryFeet
consts.comment: in a reasonably strong wind sparks and ash from a fire can be carried as far as 100 feet away

consts.name: wflRecheckTurns
consts.comment: when moving in hopes of a better camp spot, the DM allows further fuel checks every two turns

consts.name: wflTerrainCount
consts.comment: the temperate Table 39 grid covers five terrains: desert, forest, hills, plains and swamp

consts.name: wflClimateTerrainCount
consts.comment: the climate modifier grid covers six terrains: desert, forest, hills, mountains, plains and swamp

bools.name: wflStartAssumesTools
bools.comment: the start discipline assumes the character has the tools for fire-starting (flint and steel, and a tinderbox) and the fuel is dry and easy to ignite

bools.name: wflHardStartOnWindOrWet
bools.comment: if the wind velocity is greater than 15 mph or the fuel is wet, the time needed to start the fire is 3d20 instead of 2d20, plus the extra time for a medium or large fire

bools.name: wflUnskilledNeedsTools
bools.comment: a character without proficiency in fire-building cannot start a fire without the aid of tools

bools.name: wflRefuelKeepsSize
bools.comment: refuel, expressed in turns, is how often a fire fuel must be replenished for it to remain at a certain size

bools.name: wflUnrefueledShrinks
bools.comment: a fire not refueled at least this often will shrink to a fire of the next lower size

bools.name: wflSmallFireLingersCold
bools.comment: a small fire will not go out within three turns, but it will get so small that it provides no warmth

bools.name: wflWindResUnprotectedOnly
bools.comment: wind resistance pertains only to unprotected fires or those built in front of shelters that do not keep out all the wind

bools.name: wflOverRatedWindFalters
bools.comment: in a wind greater than the indicated velocity the fire will falter and flicker, providing no warmth

bools.name: wflWindMaySpreadFire
bools.comment: there is a chance the wind will spread the fire to nearby combustible materials and may start a larger, uncontrollable fire

bools.name: wflCapDoublesPerStep
bools.comment: a fire capacity doubles for each additional 10 feet of distance

bools.name: wflCapClustersDiminish
bools.comment: if characters cluster around a fire at less than 10 feet, the fire capacity diminishes by one-third at five feet, one-half at three feet and two-thirds at one foot

bools.name: wflVisMoonlightOrDarkness
bools.comment: visibility gives the distance in yards at which a fire of the given size is visible in moonlight or darkness

bools.name: wflVisTwilightReduction
bools.comment: in twilight conditions the visibility figure is reduced by one-third

bools.name: wflVisDaylightReduction
bools.comment: in daylight the visibility figure is reduced by one-half

bools.name: wflVisNeedsClearLine
bools.comment: in all cases the viewer line of sight must be relatively unobstructed

bools.name: wflGlowThroughDenseForest
bools.comment: the glow of the fire will be seen from an equal distance even if viewed through a moderately dense forest

bools.name: wflHillBlocksLongSight
bools.comment: the fire will not be visible from a very long distance away if the viewer and the fire are on opposite sides of a steep hill

bools.name: wflSmokeRevealsInDaylight
bools.comment: in twilight or daylight the flame may not be visible from the indicated distance, but the smoke will reveal its presence nonetheless

bools.name: wflSafeDistanceIs80Degrees
bools.comment: the minimum safe distance for a certain fire is the distance at which the air temperature is raised by 80 degrees

bools.name: wflDashMeansBurned
bools.comment: an entry of a dash on the table indicates the unsafe case: an unprotected character cannot remain closer without being burned

bools.name: wflWarmthAssumesCalm
bools.comment: the warming capabilities assume the fire is not exposed to wind of more than 10 mph

bools.name: wflWindwardWarmthCut
bools.comment: if the wind on the fire is greater than 10 mph, the warmth on the side facing the wind is reduced by 5 degrees for every 10 mph or fraction thereof of additional velocity

bools.name: wflLeewardSafeAdd
bools.comment: on the side facing away from the wind the safe distance is increased by 10 feet or one increment on the table, whichever is less, for every 10 mph or fraction thereof over 10 mph

bools.name: wflNoSafeFire
bools.comment: in the outdoors there is no such thing as a safe fire

bools.name: wflUntendedFireSpreads
bools.comment: a campfire left untended for more than a few minutes or not properly extinguished can spread with amazing speed into a conflagration that may be impossible to bring back under control

bools.name: wflCardinalRulesRealWorld
bools.comment: the cardinal rules of fire safety are the same in the game universe as they are in the real world

bools.name: wflNoFireOnCombustibles
bools.comment: the first cardinal rule: do not build a fire on top of combustible material - find a large patch of bare ground, or clear the area of all living and dead vegetation, before building

bools.name: wflFuelIsWood
bools.comment: the Table 39 grids give the percentage chance that characters will be able to gather fuel (wood) for a fire from their immediate surroundings

bools.name: wflTemperateAssumed
bools.comment: the temperate grid assumes the given terrain is in a temperate climate, with the second grid supplying the modifiers for other climates

bools.name: wflMovingAllowsRechecks
bools.comment: if a fuel check indicates none can be scavenged and characters keep moving in hopes of a better spot, the DM should allow further checks every two turns
